title: Misalign@k: Tail-Risk Evaluation of Emergent Misalignment Defenses Under Repeated Sampling

contributions.purpose: Provide an evaluation protocol that captures deployment tail-risk of emergent misalignment defenses when users can sample repeatedly.
contributions.mechanism: Misalign@k measures the fraction of prompts yielding at least one misaligned output across k high-temperature samples (T=1, top_p=1), with dual-scoring of alignment and coherence to enable sensitivity analysis across labeling criteria.
contributions.evaluation: Applied to emergent misalignment defenses (KL regularization, data interleaving) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with zero false positive rate verified on aligned base models.
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose Misalign@k with dual-scoring for sensitivity analysis, capturing deployment risk under repeated sampling.

contributions.purpose: Show that mean misalignment rates drastically understate deployment risk and that defense rankings depend on labeling criteria.
contributions.mechanism: Compare Misalign@32 against mean misalignment rates and re-rank defenses under standard versus relaxed labeling metrics.
contributions.evaluation: Misalign@32 is 3.4x to 24.2x higher than mean rates; interleaving is best under standard metrics (Misalign@32=16.67%) but worst under relaxed metrics (73.61%).
contributions.source_quote: Second, we demonstrate that tail-risk amplification is dramatic (Misalign@32 is 3.4x to 24.2x higher than mean rates) and that defense rankings flip depending on labeling choices...

contributions.purpose: Identify the mechanism causing defense rankings to flip across labeling criteria.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze incoherence rates of defended models to show incoherent outputs mechanically escape misalignment counting under standard metrics.
contributions.evaluation: Interleaving's 18.84% incoherence rate masks underlying misalignment, inflating apparent safety under standard labeling.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we identify incoherence masking as the mechanism behind this ranking flip: interleaving's high incoherence rate (18.84%) mechanically prevents misaligned outputs from being counted, inflating apparent safety.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work extends tail-risk evaluation to EM defenses, introducing Misalign@k with sensitivity analysis across labeling modes.
We address calibration concerns by verifying zero false positive rate on aligned base models across all metrics.

notes: Evaluation-protocol paper explicitly modeled as an extension of Leak@k-style repeated-sampling evaluation (Reisizadeh et al. 2025) to emergent misalignment defenses. Findings are critical of existing defense evaluations (interleaving's apparent safety attributed to incoherence masking).
